name: GA-10
label: Likely R

key_factors: District leans about eleven points Republican and Republicans hold the seat's fundamentals
Houston Gaines out-raises Pam Delancy roughly one hundred to one, with about $1.5 million in outside support
Prediction markets price Democratic chances at only a few percent
Open seat with no public polling adds uncertainty
model.rationale: The district's eleven-point Republican lean, Gaines's overwhelming fundraising edge, and market pricing near 95 percent Republican all point the same way. The open seat and a potentially Democratic-leaning midterm year keep the race from reaching the safe column.
model.watch: A strong Democratic national wave or an unexpected Republican stumble could pull the margin into single digits.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Mike Collins (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Georgia's 10th District, anchored in Athens and stretching toward Augusta, has been held by Mike Collins since 2023 and leans about eleven points Republican. Collins is leaving the seat to run for Senate, creating an open contest, but Republicans landed a strong recruit in Houston Gaines.

Gaines has raised about $2.3 million and draws roughly $1.5 million in outside support, while Democrat Pam Delancy has raised about $23,000 with no outside spending in the race. No public polls cover the contest, and prediction markets give Democrats only a slim chance. A favorable midterm environment could narrow the gap, but the district's lean and the lopsided money race point to a comfortable Republican hold.
